headline: Python vs Rust: Why Python's Lead Is Unshakable
summary: TIOBE and PyPI benchmarks confirm Python's dominant market position. Rust excels in systems programming but cannot overcome Python's vast ecosystem moat in data science, web, and education. Developers should choose based on domain fit, not hype.

slides.title: Python's Unshakable Lead Over Rust
slides.subtitle: TIOBE & PyPI data reveals why Python remains dominant
slides.body: Despite Rust's rise, Python's ecosystem moat keeps it ahead. What do the benchmarks really show?
slides.deep_dive: TIOBE measures search-engine popularity; PyPI tracks package downloads. Both show Python at #1 with a massive, mature library ecosystem. Rust ranks lower but grows steadily in niche domains. The gap reflects decades of compounding network effects, not just language features.
slides.key_fact: Python leads in popularity and package ecosystem size.
slides.why_it_matters: Engineers must choose tools based on ecosystem maturity, not just language features.

slides.title: Rust's Momentum vs Python's Entrenchment
slides.body: Rust gains in systems programming, but Python's data science and web foothold is massive. Economic drivers favor incumbent ecosystems.
slides.key_fact: Python dominates high-value domains: AI/ML, web backends, scripting, education.
slides.why_it_matters: Switching costs for organizations are prohibitive; new projects still default to Python.

slides.title: Memory Safety Without Garbage Collection
slides.body: Rust's ownership model enables performance-critical code. Python's C-extensions bridge performance gaps. Different technical philosophies.

steps.title: Rust: Compile-time ownership
steps.desc: Borrow checker enforces memory safety at build time, zero runtime cost.

steps.title: Python: Runtime flexibility
steps.desc: Garbage collector manages memory; C-extensions handle heavy lifting.

steps.title: Result: Different sweet spots
steps.desc: Rust for control; Python for velocity and ecosystem leverage.

slides.key_fact: Rust solves memory safety without GC; Python trades raw speed for developer speed.
slides.why_it_matters: Technical trade-offs dictate domain fit, not universal superiority.

slides.title: Complementary Strongholds, Minimal Overlap
slides.body: Python dominates high-level applications; Rust excels in low-level control. Overlap is minimal.
slides.key_fact: Python's package count dwarfs Rust's; Rust wins where C/C++ once ruled.
slides.why_it_matters: Teams adopt Rust for new infrastructure, keep Python for product logic.

slides.title: Choosing the Right Tool for the Job
slides.body: New projects: Python for speed of development and ecosystem; Rust for performance-critical components. Hybrid approaches are common.
slides.key_fact: Most successful teams use both: Python orchestrates, Rust accelerates.
slides.why_it_matters: Skill investment should match domain: Python for breadth, Rust for depth.

slides.title: Coexistence, Not Replacement
slides.body: Python's moat is deep; Rust expands the frontier. The future is polyglot, not winner-take-all.
takeaways: Python's ecosystem moat is deep and wide — no near-term replacement.
Rust is complementary, not a substitute, for most Python use cases.
Invest in Python for productivity; adopt Rust for specific performance needs.
